q: 1. The curved swellings from the growth of layers or wounds left after branches are cut off in an irregular manner are known as .....
explain: Rind galls are curved swellings formed where the growth of layers over wounds (left by branches cut off irregularly) takes place.

q: 2. First class timber has an average life of .....
explain: First class timber (like teak) is durable and has an average life of more than 10 years.

q: 3. Dry rot .....
explain: Dry rot, caused by fungus, reduces timber to a dry powder.

q: 4. Plywood is normally available .....
explain: As per the answer key, option d. Note: this thickness refers to a plywood sheet of the given range in the book.

q: 5. Plywood is made from .....
explain: As per the answer key, option c. Note: plywood is normally made from thin veneers of various woods, so this key answer looks doubtful.

q: 6. Fibre boards can be .....
explain: As per the answer key, option d. Note: fibre boards can also be painted and distempered, so the question is ambiguous in the book.

q: 7. The cracks which extend from bark towards the sap wood in the cross section of a tree, are called .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b (star shakes): cracks radiating from the bark inwards, wider at the circumference.

q: 8. The cracks caused by shrinkage of the exterior surface of the wood exposed to atmosphere are called .....
explain: As per the answer key, option c. Shrinkage of the outer surface on exposure to the atmosphere causes surface cracks (wind cracks).

q: 9. The solution of salts from the soil absorbed by the trees which becomes a viscous solution due to loss of moisture and action of carbon dioxide is known as .....
explain: The solution of salts absorbed from the soil, which thickens as moisture is lost and CO2 acts on it, is sap.

q: 10. The age of the tree can be judged from .....
explain: One annual ring is added each year, so counting them gives the age of the tree.

q: 11. Inner part of a timber log surrounding the pith is called .....
explain: The dark inner part around the pith is the heartwood.

q: 12. Age of tree may be ascertained by .....
explain: One ring forms per year, so the number of annual rings gives the age.

q: 13. Seasoning of timber is essential to remove .....
explain: Seasoning removes sap and moisture from timber to prevent decay and shrinkage.

q: 14. A piece of sawn timber whose cross-sectional dimensions exceed 5 cm, in one direction and ... cm in the other direction, is called a .....
explain: A baulk is a large sawn timber piece. Part of the question text is cut off in the scan, so the missing number is shown as '...' and I could not verify it. The answer key gives c.

q: 15. Apiece of timber whose thickness and width are respectively 5 cm and 10 cm is called .....
explain: As per the answer key, such a small section piece is called a strip.

q: 16. Seasoning of timber is done .....
explain: Seasoning removes water (sap and moisture) from timber.

q: 17. An assembled product made up of veneers and adhesives is called .....
explain: Plywood is made by gluing thin veneers together.

q: 18. In a well-seasoned piece of wood, the percentage of moisture present should be
explain: Well-seasoned timber typically retains a moisture content of about 10-12%, in equilibrium with atmospheric humidity.

q: 19. The thickness of five-ply sheet varies from .....
explain: As per the answer key, five-ply sheets are 6 to 9 mm thick.

q: 20. The usual thickness of plywood board for 3-ply is
explain: A standard 3-ply plywood board typically has a thickness in the range of 3 to 5 mm.

q: 21. The thickness of lamin boards vary from .....
explain: As per the answer key, laminboards are 12 to 25 mm thick.

q: 22. The average weight of sandal wood is
explain: Sandalwood, being a dense hardwood, has an average unit weight of about 865 kg/m3 (as per the reference table).

q: 23. The wood generally used for railway sleepers is .....
explain: As per the answer key, kail is generally used for railway sleepers.

q: 24. Which one of the following does not belong to exogenous trees .....
explain: Shisham, teak and sal are exogenous; coconut is endogenous, so it is the one that does not belong. In the book the options are printed in the order a, c, b, d (coconut, teak, shisham, sal), and the key gives a, coconut.

q: 25. Which of the following trees yields hard wood?
explain: Shisham is a hardwood (from broad-leaved trees). Deodar, chir and pine are softwoods from conifers.

q: 26. Which of the following is used to fill up the pores of wood?
explain: As given in the source answer key, this filler material is used to fill and seal the pores of wood before finishing.

q: 27. Plywood is obtained from
explain: Teak wood, being durable and stable, is commonly used to manufacture plywood veneers.

q: 28. Which of the following is usually costliest?
explain: Cellulose paint, requiring specialized processing and rapid-drying solvents, is generally the most expensive of these options.

q: 29. Plywood is defined by its
explain: Plywood is commercially specified and defined primarily by its thickness.

q: 30. Due to attack of dry rot, the timber .....
explain: Dry rot reduces timber to powder.

q: 31. Teak wood is suitable for .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Note: teak is also used for sleepers, so the key answer is debatable.

q: 32. Seasoning of timber is done for .....
explain: Seasoning is done to decrease the moisture content of timber.

q: 33. Veneering means .....
options: carving out designs on timber planks
thick layer of superior wood glued to inferior wood
thin layer of superior wood glued to inferior wood
explain: Veneering is gluing a thin layer of superior wood on an inferior wood base.

q: 34. Plywood is made from
explain: Plywood can be manufactured from a variety of wood sources including common timber, teak, and bamboo veneers.

q: 35. Which of the following defect in timber is caused either by a root of a branch or tissues set in elliptical or concentric circles?
explain: Ring-galls are defects formed by tissue growth in elliptical or concentric patterns, often originating from a branch root.

q: 36. Generally wooden moulds are made from .....
explain: As per the answer key, shisham wood, which is hard and durable. (The book prints 'play wood' in option a.)

q: 37. Cross cut saw is used for
explain: A cross cut saw, fitted with hardened teeth, is designed specifically for cutting hard stones.

q: 38. Sapwood consists of
options: innermost annular rings around the pith
portion of timber between heartwood and cambium layer
thin fibers which extends from the pith outwards and holds and annular rings together
explain: Sapwood is the living, outer portion of the tree trunk located between the heartwood and the cambium layer.

q: 39. Which of the following trees yields hard wood?
explain: Shishum is a hardwood tree, unlike deodar, chir, and pine, which yield softwood timber.

q: 40. Which of the following timbers is suitable for making sports goods
explain: Sal wood's strength and toughness make it suitable for manufacturing sports goods.

q: 41. Plywood has the advantage of
options: greater tensile strength in linger direction
greater tensile strength in shorter direction
same tensile strength in all direction
explain: Since plywood layers are cross-bonded with alternating grain directions, it achieves uniform tensile strength in all directions.

q: 42. In which of the following directions, the strength of timber is maximum
explain: Timber is strongest when loaded parallel to its grain, along the direction of its fiber structure.

q: 43. The age of a tree can be known by examining
explain: Each annual growth cycle forms one annular (growth) ring, so counting them reveals the tree's age.

q: 44. Plywood is made by bonding together thin layers of wood in such a way that the angle between grains of any layer to grains of adjacent layers is
explain: Plywood layers are bonded with grains at 90 degrees to each other, which balances strength across both directions.

q: 45. The artificial seasoning of timber may
explain: Seasoning is the process of removing the sap or moisture from timber to prevent decay and improve its stability for construction.

q: 46. Which one of the following does not belong to endogenous trees?
explain: Endogenous trees grow inwards (like bamboo or palm). Teak is an exogenous tree, meaning it grows outwards by adding annual rings.

q: 47. Which one of the following does not belong to exogenous trees?
explain: Coconut is an endogenous tree; its fibers are distributed throughout the stem rather than growing in concentric rings.

q: 48. The solution of salts from the soil absorbed by the trees which becomes a viscous solution due to loss of moisture and action of carbon dioxide is known as
explain: As per Key b but Sap is the fluid that circulates through a plant's vascular system, carrying nutrients and water.

q: 49. The no. of annual ring in a log of 30 then life of the timber is
explain: Since one annual ring generally represents one year of growth, 30 rings indicate a tree life of 30 years.

q: 50. The layer between the bark of the tree and the sap wood which is not yet converted into wood is called
explain: The cambium layer is the thin layer of living cells between the inner bark and the sapwood where new wood and bark cells are produced.
